info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Generated from the live router — every operation below is a route the unified cloud binary actually serves. Tagged by product: the first path segment after /v1/.

get.summary: listAccounts returns the caller org's connected channels, optionally narrowed to
get.description:
listAccounts returns the caller org's connected channels, optionally narrowed to
one network.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Provider narrows to one network (x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube, threads); empty means every connected account.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: createAccount records a connected social channel for the caller's org.
post.description:
createAccount records a connected social channel for the caller's org. Provider
defaults to x and must be one this deployment knows; status defaults to connected.
The id and timestamps of the input are ignored — the server assigns them. No OAuth
is performed here: this stores the channel, it does not authorize it.

delete.summary: deleteAccount disconnects a channel and answers 204.
delete.description:
deleteAccount disconnects a channel and answers 204. Posts already published
through it are left as they are.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: getAccount returns one of the caller org's connected channels.
get.description:
getAccount returns one of the caller org's connected channels. An account in
another org reads as not found. The provider token is never serialized.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

put.summary: updateAccount replaces a connected channel's provider, handle and status.
put.description:
updateAccount replaces a connected channel's provider, handle and status. Every
field is rewritten from the input, so send the whole record. The stored provider
token is untouched.

get.summary: listPosts returns the caller org's posts, optionally narrowed to one lifecycle
get.description:
listPosts returns the caller org's posts, optionally narrowed to one lifecycle
state.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status narrows to one lifecycle state (draft, scheduled, published, failed);
empty means every post.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the rows returned; 0 means 200 and nothing above 1000 is honoured.

post.summary: createPost writes a post for the caller's org.
post.description:
createPost writes a post for the caller's org. Content is required; channel
defaults to x and status to draft. A post created as scheduled for now or earlier
publishes immediately and comes back carrying that outcome; one scheduled for the
future is left to the scheduler. A failed publish never fails the create — the post
exists either way.

delete.summary: deletePost removes a post and answers 204.
delete.description:
deletePost removes a post and answers 204. A post already published is deleted
from the record only — nothing is retracted from the network it went out on.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary: getPost returns one of the caller org's posts, including its publish outcome.
get.description:
getPost returns one of the caller org's posts, including its publish outcome. A
post in another org reads as not found.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

put.summary: updatePost replaces a post's content, channel, status, schedule and media.
put.description:
updatePost replaces a post's content, channel, status, schedule and media. Content
is required and every field is rewritten from the input, so send the whole record.
The publish results (account, external id, error) are server-owned and untouched.

post.summary:
publishPost pushes a post to its channel's connected accounts now — the explicit
publish, twin of the on-create fanout.
post.description:
publishPost pushes a post to its channel's connected accounts now — the explicit
publish, twin of the on-create fanout. Idempotent: an already-published post comes
back unchanged. A push the deployment cannot make answers 503 naming exactly which
credentials are missing; a provider that rejects the push is recorded on the post as
failed and returned, never reported as a server fault.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

get.summary:
listProviders reports each network's publish-readiness: whether this deployment
holds that network's OAuth-app credentials and, when it does not, exactly which
environment variables are missing.
get.description:
listProviders reports each network's publish-readiness: whether this deployment
holds that network's OAuth-app credentials and, when it does not, exactly which
environment variables are missing. Read live from the environment, never fabricated.

get.summary: summary reports the caller org's post counts by state and how many channels are
get.description:
summary reports the caller org's post counts by state and how many channels are
connected.

data.description: Data is the page; an empty array when the org has connected no account.

accountId.description:
AccountID / ExternalID / Error are server-managed publish results, set only by
the publish path (never by a client update): the account a post was published
through, the provider's returned external post id (for reconciliation), and the
last failure reason. Empty until a publish attempt lands.

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as a list of URLs (images today; the
composer's URL field now, an S3 picker later, populate it). Stored as a JSON
array in the media TEXT column and ALWAYS serialized as an array (never null),
so a client can rely on `media` being present. Bounded at the write layer
(normMedia in social.go): each URL clipped to maxField, the list to maxMedia.

data.description: Data is the page; an empty array when the org has written no post.
Data is one row per supported network, in the fixed provider order.

id.description: ID is the record id from the path, as returned by create.

accounts.description: Accounts is how many channels are connected.

posts.description: Posts is how many posts the org has, in any state.

published.description: Published is how many have gone out.

scheduled.description: Scheduled is how many are waiting for their send time.
